pages.title: Eleven dollars and fifty cents · 1/3
paragraphs: It is lunch time at a small cafe in Denver. The line is short, and the cafe is warm. Ray has a tray with a sandwich and a salad. He walks to the counter and smiles. Ana, the cashier, looks at the screen. She says the total in a friendly voice.
“That is eleven dollars and fifty cents.” says Ana. “Here is a twenty-dollar bill.” says Ray. “Your change is eight fifty.” says Ana.

pages.title: Laboratório de sons · o som
pages.what: Em change, o “ch” é “tch”. Em cash, o final “sh” é um sopro contínuo. Muitos brasileiros trocam um pelo outro.
pages.how: Em change, junte a língua ao céu da boca e solte: “tcheinj”. Em cash, termine com ar contínuo: “késh”.
pages.tip: Peça silêncio com “shhh” para cash e faça “tch” de espirro para change.
